assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is oven thermal behavior and setup for cupcakes, finer than a whole-baking KB
a standard home or small bakeshop oven with a thermostat and optional convection fan is assumed
recipe formulation, batter chemistry, and frosting are referenced only where heat interacts with them
exclusions: batter formulation, leavening chemistry, and mixing method internals

competency_questions.question: What is the oven's true cavity temperature versus its dial readout?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OVEN_CAL_OFFSET and TRUE_TEMP_PROBE define measured offset

competency_questions.question: How much does true temperature swing as the heating element cycles?
When is the oven truly soaked and ready to load for good oven spring?
How do thermal mass, door openings, and lag affect recovery and pull timing?
Which rack and loading layout give even color across the batch?
How are hot spots and radiant overload detected and corrected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOTSPOT_MAP and RADIANT_SHIELDING cover detection and fix

competency_questions.question: When should convection be used and how is its setpoint adjusted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONVECTION_MODE and CONVECTION_TEMP_DROP cover choice and adjustment

competency_questions.question: How do pan material, color, and liner change heat transfer to the cupcake?
Which liner releases cleanly while still setting the cupcake edge?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LINER_CHOICE covers release and edge set

competency_questions.question: How full should liners be for a level, fully set crown?
How is cavity humidity managed so crowns set without skinning or tackiness?
Which heat-transfer mode dominates a given setup and how is the bake fixed?
When should a cupcake be pulled given lag, carryover, and element cycling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THERMAL_LAG_TIMING and ELEMENT_CYCLING cover pull timing

competency_questions.question: How are hot pans and cooling handled safely without unsafe warm holding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OVEN_SAFE_HANDLING covers safe handling and cooling

glossary.definition: signed difference between true cavity temperature and the dial setpoint
heat capacity of cavity, racks, and ballast that buffers temperature changes
early rapid rise as gases expand before the crumb structure sets
forced-air heat transfer from a fan that evens color and speeds set
filling liners to about two-thirds capacity for a level, set crown
continued internal baking from retained heat after the pan leaves the oven
temperature band where pathogens multiply and warm food must not be held

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for oven thermodynamics and setup work units, grounded in standard baking-science references in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: general baking-science consensus (McGee On Food and Cooking; Lopez-Alt The Food Lab; Figoni How Baking Works; Myhrvold Modernist Cuisine)

nodes.definition: Measure the oven's true vs dial temperature and record a per-setting offset used by every bake decision.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven serviced, moved, or thermostat replaced

pros.claim: Anchors every temperature-dependent step to real cavity heat
pros.example: dial 350F reads 325F true; offset prevents pale dense cupcakes

cons.claim: A wrong or stale offset silently miscalibrates the whole bake
cons.example: uncaught +30F offset over-browns crowns before centers set

acceptance_tests: offset measured at 3 setpoints with a soaked thermometer

nodes.definition: Place a calibrated independent thermometer in the cavity to read true bake temperature rather than trusting the readout.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: thermometer dropped or fails ice-point check

pros.claim: Gives ground truth that the offset table depends on
pros.example: probe shows 18F swing as element cycles

cons.claim: A miscalibrated probe poisons the offset it feeds
cons.example: cheap dial probe reads 15F high, baking too cool

failure_modes: probe near a hot spot biasing reading
acceptance_tests: probe verified at ice point before use

nodes.definition: Preheat the oven fully and soak the cavity and racks so walls radiate steadily before cupcakes go in.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven model with faster/slower recovery

pros.claim: Loading into a fully soaked cavity gives consistent oven spring
pros.example: walls at temp drive even doming vs a cold-wall pale set

cons.claim: Trusting the preheat beep loads too early into an under-soaked cavity
cons.example: beep at 5 min but walls still 40F low

acceptance_tests: true temp held at setpoint for soak window before load

nodes.definition: Manage oven thermal mass and temperature recovery after the door opens and cold batter loads.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: adding or removing a baking steel/stone

pros.claim: High thermal mass buffers the temp drop when cold pans load
pros.example: steel ballast holds temp so early set is stable

cons.claim: Too much mass slows recovery and over-soaks the bottom
cons.example: heavy stone scorches liner bottoms

acceptance_tests: recovery time to setpoint measured after a full load

nodes.definition: Select the rack height that balances radiant top/bottom heat for even cupcake rise and crown color.

included: center vs upper vs lower rack

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: different oven element configuration

pros.claim: Center rack balances top and bottom radiant load for level crowns
pros.example: center slot avoids scorched bottoms and pale tops

cons.claim: Wrong rack overexposes one face to a glowing element
cons.example: top rack browns crowns before centers set

acceptance_tests: rack slot chosen and justified by element layout

nodes.definition: Map cavity hot and cold spots and define a rotation schedule so cupcakes bake to uniform color.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven develops new hot spot or fan changes

pros.claim: Rotating at the right moment evens out a known hot corner
pros.example: half-turn at 60% bake levels back-row browning

cons.claim: Rotating too early collapses delicate crowns mid-set
cons.example: opening at 5 min drops uncrowned tops

acceptance_tests: hot-spot map produced from a uniform test bake

nodes.definition: Decide convection (forced air) vs conventional (still air) baking for the target crumb, crown and color.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recipe wants flatter or domier crowns

pros.claim: Convection evens multi-rack color and speeds set
pros.example: fan bake browns 24 cupcakes uniformly across two racks

cons.claim: Forced air dries crowns and can lean or skin them early
cons.example: high fan skins tops before they rise, cracking domes

failure_modes: running full fan on delicate batters
acceptance_tests: mode chosen with rationale for crumb and crown target

nodes.definition: Apply the convection temperature reduction (about 25F / 15C) and time adjustment so forced air does not over-bake.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven auto-compensates fan temp already

pros.claim: Dropping setpoint for fan prevents over-browned dry crowns
pros.example: 350 conventional -> 325 convection keeps crumb moist

cons.claim: Double-compensating an auto-adjusting oven under-bakes centers
cons.example: oven already drops 25F and baker drops again, raw centers

acceptance_tests: adjusted setpoint derived from rule and offset

nodes.definition: Choose muffin pan material (heavy aluminized steel vs thin steel vs silicone) for conduction to the batter.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: switching pan stock or to silicone

pros.claim: Heavy aluminized steel conducts evenly for a clean set bottom
pros.example: aluminized pan avoids gummy under-set centers

cons.claim: Silicone insulates and under-sets bottoms and sidewalls
cons.example: silicone tray leaves pale, weak cupcake sides

failure_modes: using insulated pans for tender batters
acceptance_tests: pan material chosen for target bottom set

nodes.definition: Account for pan color and finish (dark/nonstick absorbs more radiant heat than shiny light) when setting temperature.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: switching between dark and light pans

pros.claim: Dropping temp for dark pans prevents scorched bottoms
pros.example: dark nonstick at -15F avoids burnt liner bottoms

cons.claim: Ignoring finish over-browns dark pans or under-browns shiny ones
cons.example: shiny pan leaves pale bottoms at normal temp

failure_modes: baking dark pans at light-pan temps

nodes.definition: Select cupcake liner material and color (paper, foil, greaseproof, dark vs light) for release and heat transfer to the edge.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: liner stock or color changes

pros.claim: Foil liners conduct edge heat and resist greasy bleed-through
pros.example: foil cups set firmer cupcake sidewalls

cons.claim: Thick dark liners insulate or absorb unevenly, mottling edges
cons.example: dark thick paper leaves pale, soft edges

acceptance_tests: liner chosen for release and edge set

nodes.definition: Fill liners to about two-thirds so heat penetrates to the center before edges over-set, giving a level crown.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: different liner size or batter density

pros.claim: Two-thirds fill lets centers set before edges dry, giving a domed crown
pros.example: 2/3 scoop yields a level dome, not a sunken or spilled top

cons.claim: Overfilling spills and bakes a mushroomed dense crown
cons.example: brim fill overflows and sets a gummy center

acceptance_tests: fill target set near two-thirds with a portion scoop

nodes.definition: Manage cavity steam and humidity from batter moisture and venting so crowns set without skinning or staying tacky.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: large batch raises cavity humidity

pros.claim: Right humidity lets crowns rise glossy before skinning
pros.example: slight vent prevents a tacky uncrowned top

cons.claim: Too much trapped steam keeps crowns tacky and pale
cons.example: sealed cavity in a big batch leaves wet skins

acceptance_tests: venting/humidity choice documented for batch size

nodes.definition: Balance the three heat-transfer modes (conduction from pan, convection from air, radiation from elements) for even bake.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any pan, rack, or mode change shifts the balance

pros.claim: Naming the dominant mode explains and fixes uneven bakes
pros.example: spotting radiant-dominant top heat triggers a rack drop

cons.claim: Ignoring mode interplay leads to chasing the wrong knob
cons.example: raising temp when the real fault is pan conduction

failure_modes: treating heat as a single dial
acceptance_tests: dominant transfer mode identified for the setup

nodes.definition: Limit and time door openings so the cavity does not crash temperature and collapse rising cupcakes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven with poor door seal or slow recovery

pros.claim: Holding the door shut until set protects oven spring
pros.example: no peeking before 70% bake keeps domes from sinking

cons.claim: Frequent opens crash temp and collapse delicate crowns
cons.example: early peek drops 40F and sinks centers

failure_modes: leaving the door open during rotation
acceptance_tests: door-open policy ties opens to set timing

nodes.definition: Decide single-rack vs multi-rack loading and tray spacing so airflow and radiant heat reach every cupcake.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: larger batch forces multi-rack

pros.claim: Convection plus staggered trays bakes two racks evenly
pros.example: staggered pans let fan air reach back rows

cons.claim: Crowding blocks airflow and radiant heat, mottling color
cons.example: crammed pans leave pale shadowed cupcakes

acceptance_tests: loading layout keeps airflow paths open
two-rack color acceptable or single-rack chosen

nodes.definition: Target the early high-heat oven-spring window where leavening expands before structure sets, for a domed crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: leavening system or setpoint changes

pros.claim: Hot soaked start drives oven spring before the crumb sets
pros.example: full preheat gives a tall, level dome

cons.claim: Too-cool start sets structure before gases expand, flat tops
cons.example: cold start yields squat, dense crowns

failure_modes: starting too cool for the leavening
acceptance_tests: setpoint and preheat tuned to the spring window

nodes.definition: Shield cupcakes from direct radiant element heat (foil tent, doubled tray, lower rack) when tops or bottoms scorch.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven with very close broiler element

pros.claim: A foil tent blocks radiant overload while centers finish
pros.example: tent at 70% bake stops crown scorching

cons.claim: Over-shielding under-browns and traps steam at the crown
cons.example: full foil cap leaves pale tacky tops

failure_modes: tenting too early and trapping steam
acceptance_tests: shielding applied to the scorching face only

nodes.definition: Account for thermal lag and carryover so cupcakes are pulled at the right internal state, not just on the timer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pan mass or batter density changes carryover

pros.claim: Pulling for carryover avoids dry over-baked centers
pros.example: pull at just-set lets carryover finish moist

cons.claim: Trusting only the timer over-bakes a hot, high-mass setup
cons.example: timer pull misses early-done centers, drying them

failure_modes: trusting the timer over true cues
acceptance_tests: pull timing adjusted for lag and carryover

nodes.definition: Account for thermostat element on/off cycling that swings true temperature around the setpoint during the bake.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: oven with wide thermostat hysteresis

pros.claim: Knowing the swing explains batch-to-batch color shifts
pros.example: loading at a cycle peak vs trough changes early set

cons.claim: Assuming flat temp misreads a wide-swinging oven
cons.example: 30F swing blamed wrongly on the recipe

acceptance_tests: cycle amplitude measured from a probe trace
revisit_triggers: batch color varies with identical settings

nodes.definition: Handle hot pans, steam bursts, and danger-zone cooling safely so the bake is delicious without burns or unsafe holding.

included: safe cooling out of danger zone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new equipment or hotter cavity

pros.claim: Safe handling prevents burns and unsafe warm holding
pros.example: mitts and a cooling rack avoid steam burns and condensation

cons.claim: Skipping safety risks burns and danger-zone holding
cons.example: bare-hand pull causes a burn and dropped tray

failure_modes: holding warm cupcakes in the danger zone
acceptance_tests: cooling moves food out of the danger zone promptly

edges.why_related: offset is computed from independent probe readings
edges.benefit_of_coupling: grounds the offset in real cavity heat
edges.example: probe drift shifts whole offset table

edges.why_related: probe confirms the cavity actually reached setpoint
edges.example: beep at 5 min but walls cold

edges.why_related: true preheat target uses the measured offset
edges.benefit_of_coupling: preheat aims at true not dial temp

edges.why_related: recovery behavior follows from how fully the cavity soaked
a hot soaked start drives early oven spring
rack choice is judged against true per-position temperature
edges.example: top rack runs hotter than read

edges.why_related: hot-spot mapping refines the chosen rack
edges.benefit_of_coupling: targets rotation on the real gradient

edges.why_related: rack height sets radiant top/bottom contribution
the temp reduction only applies once convection is chosen
mode choice sets the convective contribution
the reduced setpoint is computed off the true-temp offset
color/finish compensation layers on the base material
liner pairs with pan conduction for edge set
pan conduction is a core term in the mode balance
pan-color temp adjustment is relative to the true setpoint
fill depth and rack jointly set crown evenness
fill depth governs how heat reaches the center during spring
forced air strips cavity humidity from crowns
door-open policy protects the soaked cavity temperature
thermal mass buffers the door-open temp crash
loading layout extends single-rack choice to the full batch
multi-rack loading is viable mainly under convection
pan mass and conduction drive carryover and lag
cavity and pan mass set carryover magnitude
cycling amplitude is read from the probe trace
average vs peak temp refines the offset meaning
edges.risk_of_conflict: offset taken at a cycle peak

edges.why_related: shielding is the fix when radiant mode dominates and scorches
rack move and shielding both manage radiant overload
spring window leads into the set-and-pull timing
a fully hot oven defines the burn and steam hazards
fan evenness fights crown moisture retention
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balances even color vs glossy crown
edges.risk_of_conflict: fan dries crowns while evening color
edges.resolution_rule: if crowns skin or crack, reduce fan speed or switch to conventional; even color is subordinate to an intact moist crown

edges.why_related: more fill for bigger domes fights center heat penetration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: trades dome size vs set center
edges.resolution_rule: cap fill near two-thirds; a level fully set crumb dominates over a taller but gummy dome

edges.why_related: dark-pan radiant gain fights even gentle center doneness
edges.benefit_of_coupling: trades fast browning vs moist center
edges.risk_of_conflict: dark pan browns edge before center sets
edges.resolution_rule: lower setpoint for dark pans and pull for carryover; a moist set center dominates over fast surface color

edges.why_related: lowering fan temp for moisture fights the high heat that drives spring
edges.benefit_of_coupling: trades crumb moisture vs dome height
edges.risk_of_conflict: too low fan temp flattens crowns
edges.resolution_rule: reduce by the rule amount only (~25F); preserve enough early heat for spring, moisture is balanced not maximized

edges.why_related: packing more trays per load fights uniform color across the cavity
edges.resolution_rule: if multi-rack color fails, drop to single rack or add rotation; even color dominates over batch throughput

edges.why_related: tenting to stop scorch traps steam and tackifies crowns
edges.benefit_of_coupling: trades scorch protection vs crown set
edges.resolution_rule: tent only the scorching face and only after set; a cleanly set crown dominates over full radiant shielding

edges.why_related: safe out-of-danger-zone cooling overrides squeezing carryover bake
edges.benefit_of_coupling: trades carryover finish vs food safety
edges.risk_of_conflict: holding warm to use carryover keeps food in danger zone
edges.resolution_rule: food safety dominates: cool promptly out of the danger zone even if it slightly limits carryover finishing

conflict_axes.trigger: forced air evens color but dries and skins crowns
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if crowns skin or crack, moist-crown side dominates and fan is reduced
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: visible crown cracking or tacky skin on a test bake
conflict_axes.example: two-rack fan bake evens color but cracks domes

conflict_axes.trigger: more fill makes taller domes but undercooks the center
resolution_order: lower temp if edges scorch first
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a level fully set crumb dominates over a taller gummy dome
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: center still wet when edges fully browned
conflict_axes.example: brim-filled liners mushroom and gum the center

conflict_axes.trigger: dark pans and radiant heat brown fast before centers set moist
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a moist set center dominates over fast surface color
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: edges scorched while center reads underdone
conflict_axes.example: dark pan scorches bottoms before the crumb sets

conflict_axes.trigger: packing more trays per load speeds output but mottles color
resolution_order: drop to single rack if uneven
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: even color dominates over batch throughput when they conflict
conflict_axes.example: crammed two-rack load leaves pale shadowed cupcakes

conflict_axes.trigger: lowering fan temp to keep moisture weakens the heat that drives spring
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: preserve enough early heat for spring; moisture is balanced not maximized
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: crowns squat under reduced fan temp
conflict_axes.example: over-reduced fan temp flattens the dome

conflict_axes.trigger: tenting to stop scorch traps steam and tackifies the crown
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: a cleanly set crown dominates over full radiant shielding
conflict_axes.example: full foil cap leaves pale tacky tops

conflict_axes.trigger: high surface heat browns sugary crowns fast, risking bitter over-browning vs flavor
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: controlled browning for flavor dominates over maximum color; avoid bitter scorch
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: crown browns past golden into bitter
conflict_axes.example: top-rack high heat scorches a sweet crown bitter

conflict_axes.trigger: skipping calibration and probe checks is faster but bakes blind
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: calibration rigor dominates convenience for repeatable delicious results
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: batch results vary at identical settings
conflict_axes.example: trusting the dial saves time but yields pale dense cupcakes

conflict_axes.trigger: holding cupcakes warm to exploit carryover keeps food in the danger zone
resolution_order: let carryover finish during normal cooling
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: food safety hard-dominates: cool out of the danger zone even at the cost of carryover finishing
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any warm holding inside the danger zone
conflict_axes.example: warm-holding a tray to finish baking risks unsafe food

edge_cases.failure_mode: every bake runs at the wrong true temperature
edge_cases.example: offset measured 6 months ago now off by 20F
edge_cases.detection_method: periodic probe re-check against the offset table

edge_cases.trigger: oven beeps ready before walls and racks soak
edge_cases.failure_mode: loading into an under-soaked cavity weakens oven spring
edge_cases.example: beep at 5 min but probe still 30F low

edge_cases.trigger: oven auto-reduces fan temp and the baker reduces again
edge_cases.example: firmware drops 25F and baker drops another 25F
edge_cases.detection_method: check oven manual for auto fan compensation

edge_cases.trigger: silicone pan insulates and bottoms never set
edge_cases.example: silicone tray leaves pale under-set bottoms

edge_cases.failure_mode: batter spills and crowns mushroom over a gummy center
edge_cases.example: brim fill overflows onto the pan top
edge_cases.detection_method: scoop volume vs liner capacity check

edge_cases.trigger: dark pan baked at light-pan temperature

edge_cases.example: peek at 5 min sinks the centers

edge_cases.trigger: trays packed edge to edge blocking airflow
edge_cases.example: crammed pans leave pale back rows

edge_cases.trigger: high fan speed skins crowns before they rise
edge_cases.example: full fan cracks the crown skin

edge_cases.trigger: pull on timer ignoring carryover on a high-mass setup
edge_cases.example: heavy pan keeps baking after the timer

cupcakes held warm in the danger zone to finish baking

workflow.do_first_because: every temperature decision depends on true cavity temperature

workflow.objective: measure element on/off swing around setpoint
workflow.do_first_because: cycling explains batch-to-batch variation at identical settings

workflow.objective: fully soak cavity, racks, and ballast before loading
acceptance_tests: true temp held through soak window
workflow.do_first_because: oven spring depends on a fully soaked start

workflow.objective: choose rack and map hot spots with a rotation plan
workflow.do_first_because: placement sets the radiant balance every later step depends on

workflow.objective: pick convection vs conventional and adjust setpoint

workflow.objective: choose pan material, color compensation, and liner

priority_rationale.notes: tier=0 calibration anchors all temperature decisions
central balance of the three transfer modes

dominance_rules.trigger: warm-holding cupcakes to exploit carryover keeps food in the danger zone
dominance_rules.rule: food safety dominates: cool promptly out of the danger zone even at the cost of carryover finishing
dominance_rules.required_action: pull and cool on a rack; never warm-hold for doneness
dominance_rules.example: a tray held warm an hour to finish baking is unsafe

dominance_rules.trigger: raw egg/dairy batter or under-set centers risk pathogen survival
dominance_rules.rule: centers must reach a safe set state; do not deliberately underbake for moisture
dominance_rules.example: gummy raw center chased for moistness is not served

dominance_rules.trigger: true cavity temperature conflicts with the dial readout
dominance_rules.rule: measured true temperature dominates the dial for every decision
dominance_rules.example: 350 dial baked as 325 true via the offset

dominance_rules.trigger: even multi-rack color conflicts with an intact moist crown
dominance_rules.rule: if forced air cracks or skins crowns, reduce fan; crown integrity dominates color evenness
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce fan speed or switch to conventional
dominance_rules.example: two-rack fan bake cracking domes drops to conventional

dominance_rules.trigger: taller dome from overfill conflicts with a fully set center
dominance_rules.rule: a level fully set crumb dominates over a taller gummy dome
dominance_rules.example: brim fill mushrooms over a raw center is rejected

dominance_rules.trigger: fast surface browning conflicts with a moist set center
dominance_rules.rule: moist set center dominates over maximum surface color
dominance_rules.required_action: lower setpoint for dark pans and pull for carryover
dominance_rules.example: dark pan scorching bottoms gets a lower setpoint

dominance_rules.trigger: batch throughput conflicts with even color across the load
dominance_rules.rule: even color dominates over packing more trays per load
dominance_rules.required_action: drop to single rack or add rotation
dominance_rules.example: crammed racks mottling color revert to single rack

dominance_rules.trigger: convenience of skipping calibration conflicts with repeatable quality
dominance_rules.rule: calibration rigor dominates convenience when results must be repeatable
dominance_rules.required_action: verify offset and probe before critical batches
dominance_rules.example: trusting the dial to save time yields inconsistent bakes

anti_rework_rules.rule: measure the oven offset before choosing any bake temperature
anti_rework_rules.rationale: all temperature decisions depend on the true offset
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: setpoints chosen against the dial only

anti_rework_rules.rule: fully soak the cavity before loading any batter
anti_rework_rules.rationale: oven spring depends on a soaked start
anti_rework_rules.example: loading at 5 min with cold walls

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix rack and hot-spot plan before scaling to multi-rack loads
anti_rework_rules.rationale: placement sets the radiant balance the load depends on
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: two-rack loading without a single-rack baseline
anti_rework_rules.example: cramming two racks before mapping hot spots

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose mode and adjust setpoint before selecting vessel
anti_rework_rules.rationale: mode changes the heat balance vessel choice tunes against
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: pan chosen before mode is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: picking dark pans before deciding convection

anti_rework_rules.rule: set vessel and color compensation before filling
anti_rework_rules.rationale: vessel conduction and absorption shape fill and timing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: filling before pan finish is accounted for
anti_rework_rules.example: filling dark pans at light-pan temp

anti_rework_rules.rule: hold the door shut until crowns set
anti_rework_rules.rationale: early opens crash temperature and collapse crowns

anti_rework_rules.rule: account for carryover before fixing pull time

anti_rework_rules.example: holding warm an hour for doneness
